notes.title: Atomic Habits by James Clear
notes.html:
Atomic Habits by James Clear

Habits are the compound interest of self-improvement. Getting one percent better every day counts for a lot in the long run, even when the change is invisible at first.

You do not rise to the level of your goals. You fall to the level of your systems. Goals set a direction but a system of small habits is what produces progress.

Identity

The most effective way to change your habits is to focus on who you wish to become, not what you want to achieve. Every action is a vote for the type of person you want to be.

notes.title: Atomic Habits ch 3
notes.html:
Atomic Habits ch 3
The habit loop has four steps: cue, craving, response, and reward. The cue triggers the brain to start a behavior and the reward is the end goal of every habit.

Make it obvious, make it attractive, make it easy, and make it satisfying. These four laws of behavior change turn good habits into routines that stick.

notes.title: BIO 101 Lecture 5 notes
notes.html:
BIO 101 Lecture 5 notes

Membranes

The cell membrane is a phospholipid bilayer that controls what enters and leaves the cell. Proteins embedded in the membrane act as channels and pumps.

Transport

Diffusion moves molecules from high to low concentration without energy. Active transport uses ATP to pump ions against their gradient across the membrane.

notes.title: BIO 101 Lecture 6
notes.text:
BIO 101 Lecture 6
# Mitochondria
Mitochondria are the organelles that produce most of the cell's ATP through cellular respiration. They have their own DNA and ribosomes.
# Glycolysis
Glycolysis splits glucose into two pyruvate molecules in the cytoplasm of the cell and yields a small amount of ATP for the cell.

notes.title: Krebs cycle
notes.text:
Krebs cycle
The Krebs cycle runs inside the mitochondria of the cell. Pyruvate from glycolysis is broken down and the cycle releases carbon dioxide while producing ATP and electron carriers for the cell.

notes.title: Stoicism
notes.text:
Stoicism
The Stoic philosophy teaches that virtue is the only true good. Wisdom, justice, courage and temperance are the four virtues, and a life lived by reason in agreement with nature is a good life.

notes.title: Seneca on time 3/14
notes.text:
Seneca on time 3/14
Seneca wrote that life is long if you know how to use it. The Stoic should guard time as the most precious thing, since death takes what we waste and philosophy teaches us to live with reason and virtue.

notes.title: Startup ideas
notes.text:
Startup ideas
A tutoring marketplace for adult learners who want weekend classes. Charge a small fee per booking and grow through referrals from happy students.

notes.title: Pricing thoughts
notes.text:
Pricing thoughts
Try three tiers and anchor on the middle one. Annual plans reduce churn but the monthly plan is what most people try first before they commit.
